body: Agent harnesses require a low-latency guardrail model together with customizable audit policies. However, deploying an auto-regressive guardrail model remains challenging: such models incur high inference latency and are often poorly aligned with customized policies. To address these problems, we present Jev-Guard, a unified model for safety classification and policy routing. We further construct a policy tree over which Jev-Guard performs routing, spanning diverse domains including content moderation, cybersecurity, privacy, and legal compliance. Specifically, Jev-Guard first navigates the policy tree to select the applicable audit policy given the caller's audit context, and then performs safety classification conditioned on the retrieved policies. On 7,033 evaluation cases, Jev-Guard achieves 93.72% safety accuracy, a mean latency of 58ms, and 93.10% hierarchical routing accuracy. The full routing-and-classification pipeline averages 240ms. Furthermore, we integrate Jev-Guard into the Hermes harness framework. Across agent trajectories, its separate permission gate cuts mean review time per task from 4.80s for an SFT-LLM judge to 1.33s, with no policy violations are observed for either guard.
summaryZh: 本文介绍了Jev-Guard，一种用于智能体安全分类和策略路由的统一模型。通过构建可编辑的策略树，Jev-Guard能够根据上下文选择审计策略并进行安全分类。实验表明，该模型在保持高准确率的同时，显著降低了推理延迟，并将智能体任务的平均审核时间从4.80秒缩短至1.33秒，为构建高效、可控的智能体护栏提供了有效方案。
